title: Recruiters should spend the day talking to people, not retyping CVs.

blocks.text: Recruiters should spend the day talking to people, not retyping CVs.
Most of a recruiter's week goes to admin around the conversations that earn the fee. These are the workflows that remove the admin, with the recruiter still choosing who goes to the client.
CVs arrive in every shape
PDFs, Word files, LinkedIn exports and email bodies all get retyped into the ATS, and the record is only as good as the person's patience that day.
Shortlisting is keyword luck
Boolean searches miss good candidates who describe their work differently, and the talent pool from last quarter's roles sits unused.
Candidates and clients go quiet
Status updates depend on someone remembering. A candidate waiting a week for news often accepts another offer.
Data sits in three systems
The ATS, the CRM and the inbox each hold part of the story, so nobody sees the full history of a candidate or a client.

What should stay human
Hiring decisions affect people's livelihoods and carry legal duties. These stay with humans.
Who gets hired or rejected
The system ranks and explains. A recruiter decides who moves forward, and a human sends every rejection.
Fairness and bias review
Rankings should be audited by people against your own equal opportunity policy and local rules. We build logs that make this possible, and we do not claim a system is bias free.
Candidate relationships
Calls that persuade a hesitant candidate or calm a nervous client are the job. We remove the admin around them.
Consent and data retention
Reactivation only uses candidates with valid consent, and retention rules are set by your data protection lead.
